title: Chick Webb the epitome
summary: After a break Jones praises Chick Webb's sense of timing and his several arrangements of one tune.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, we had a little breather, session. That's beautiful, man, you have some beautiful advice there. I think we can just about close this drum section. You just happened to mention to me that we hadn't mentioned Chick Webb...

Well, you know they always say the first should be last, the last should be first. Speaking about Chick Webb, I don't speak of Chick Webb the drummer. I speak of Chick Webb the epitomé. You see, with all the phases that we have to play in, music, we're strictly in the contributing phases of the jazz idiom. Now, Mr. Chick Webb's sense of timing - he didn't settle for nothing but the best. Mr. Chick Webb would get one arrangement but he also had two more arrangements. In other words, when he had one arrangement he had three arrangements, because he might play it this way at 9 o'clock; at 12 o'clock he'd play it another; at 2 o'clock he'd play it another way, the same tune. But he had music for all occasions, as you call it. Mr. Webb had something along with his leadership and he had to be a natural, a great natural, like what we know today as a Erroll Garner It's impossible to write, to study, to do whatever. Having the responsibility that he had and not thinking so much about the economic, not thinking about the glory and what have you, and to be able to handle the group of men that was in his band.
